Prevention: Aphids are highly reproductive, small insects that can weaken plant structures and transmit virus to crops.
Avoid planting near an infested crop or on land with a history of infestation.
Active removal of weeds from plots to reduce aphid hosts.

Intercropping with pest repellent plants such as onion, garlic and parsley to reduce aphid populations close to rape.
Do not apply high levels of nitrogenous fertilizer as this will make the plants more attractive to aphids.
Monitoring: Regularly check for leaf curling on crop at leats once a week.
Observe underside of leaves for aphid presence.
Aphids are small insects of 2 mm long, soft-bodied and green, brown or yellow in colour.
High levels of infestation may result in the presence of black sooty mould on leaves due to honeydew secretion from aphids.
Monitoring should be undertaken soon after crop emergence until crop harvest.
If there is no presence of aphid-transmitted viruses in the area, small aphid populations are tolerable amongst crop.
If infestation grows (10-20% por 1-2 infested plants per 10-20 observed) then consider undertaking direct control measures.
Direct Control: Prune leaves showing symptoms (curling, aphid populations on underside).
Removal and burning of infested crops to prevent spread of the fungus.
Spray neem oil products once a week for 4 weeks (4.5 ml/10 m2).
Contact your local agro-input supplier to organise access of such products.
Use of soap water solution spray on crops to wash off any aphids present (1 tablespoons of liquid soap per 10 litres of water)
